summary: Extraction pass over 20 stored US documents (State Department Visa Office Tables V and VI for FY2005-FY2008, DHS yearbooks 2013 and 2023, two DHS OIG reports, two Behring court orders, trumpcard.gov, five DOJ press releases). Adds EB-5 visa counts for every foreign state of chargeability, with class splits (C5/T5/R5/I5), dependent-area TOTAL rows and region totals, for FY2005-FY2008 (all class, region and grand totals add up); EB-5 LPR counts by detailed class and by new arrival / adjustment from the yearbooks; regional-center application decisions, counts and fees, processing times, cumulative investment and jobs claims from the OIG reports; Gold Card terms; and two case-level misuse figures for the Jay Peak case.

observations.location: PDF p. 13 (printed p. 9), Foreign Investments and Job Creation
observations.quote: Recently, USCIS reported that since 1990, more than $6.8 billion has been invested in the U.S. economy through the EB-5 program
observations.notes: USCIS figure relayed by the DHS OIG ('more than', so a lower bound), cumulative since 1990 to shortly before December 2013. The OIG asked for support and USCIS could not provide it: USCIS said it estimated the figure assuming the programme's minimum requirements were met. '$' in a US federal report on US investment.

observations.location: PDF p. 13 (printed p. 9), Foreign Investments and Job Creation
observations.quote: and a minimum of 49,000 jobs have been created
observations.notes: USCIS figure relayed by the DHS OIG ('a minimum of'), cumulative since 1990. USCIS could not support it; it was estimated by assuming each investor met the minimum job-creation requirement.

observations.location: PDF p. 31, Appendix B (USCIS management comments, 4 Nov 2013), memo p. 7
observations.quote: denied 63 regional center applications for failure to satisfy the job creation or other eligibility requirements and approved 35 regional center applications
observations.notes: Regional center applications approved by USCIS in FY2012, stated by the USCIS Director in the management response printed in the report. The appendix is a scan; the text layer reads the agency name as 'USClS'.

observations.location: PDF p. 31, Appendix B (USCIS management comments, 4 Nov 2013), memo p. 7
observations.quote: denied 63 regional center applications for failure to satisfy the job creation or other eligibility requirements
observations.notes: Regional center applications denied by USCIS in FY2012 'for failure to satisfy the job creation or other eligibility requirements', stated by the USCIS Director in the management response.

observations.location: PDF p. 23 (printed p. 19), Appendix A
observations.quote: We identified 336 I-924 regional centers with applications or amendments submitted during fiscal years 2010, 2011, and 2012.
observations.notes: Counts regional centers (not applications) that submitted a Form I-924 designation application or amendment in FY2010-FY2012, from the USCIS iCLAIMS database as of 29 Nov 2012; the OIG did not verify the reliability of iCLAIMS.

observations.location: PDF p. 7 (printed p. 3), Application Process; repeated PDF p. 15 (printed p. 11)
observations.quote: regional centers generally collect unregulated management and administrative fees between $25,000 and $50,000 from each foreign investor
observations.notes: Range of unregulated management and administrative fees regional centers 'generally' collect from each investor (travel, marketing, legal fees, sales commissions), per USCIS documents seen by the OIG; on top of the investment. Not set by government.

observations.location: PDF p. 11 (printed p. 9), Background
observations.quote: According to USCIS, as of March 2, 2015, USCIS had approved approximately 641 regional centers.
observations.notes: USCIS figure relayed by the DHS OIG; rounded ('approximately').

observations.location: PDF p. 14 (printed p. 12), EB-5 Application and Petition Process
observations.quote: In fiscal year 2012, 6,041 immigrant investor petitions were filed in this program
observations.notes: Form I-526 investor petitions filed in FY2012, relayed by the DHS OIG (no source given). Same value as the USCIS I-526 data already in the dataset.

observations.location: PDF p. 14 (printed p. 12), EB-5 Application and Petition Process
observations.quote: USCIS granted 3,677 petitions for temporary residency
observations.notes: Form I-526 investor petitions approved in FY2012 ('petitions for temporary residency', i.e. leading to conditional residence), relayed by the DHS OIG. Same value as the USCIS I-526 data.

observations.location: PDF p. 14 (printed p. 12), EB-5 Application and Petition Process
observations.quote: In that same year, 736 alien investors were granted permanent residency status.
observations.notes: Worded as investors granted (unconditional) permanent residency in FY2012, i.e. Form I-829 approvals; matches the USCIS I-829 approvals for FY2012 already in the dataset. Relayed by the DHS OIG.

observations.location: PDF p. 8 (printed p. 6), Extraordinary Focus on a Handful of Matters
observations.quote: The EB-5 program has hundreds of existing regional centers and, in the three years in question, received more than 700 applications for regional centers.
observations.notes: 'More than 700' regional center applications 'in the three years in question'; the report does not say which three years (the matters investigated ran from 2010 to 2013, Mr. Mayorkas was USCIS Director 2009-2013). A lower bound.

observations.location: PDF p. 12 (printed p. 10), EB-5 Application and Petition Process
observations.quote: collect unregulated management and administrative fees between $25,000 and $50,000 from each foreign investor
observations.notes: Range of unregulated management and administrative fees regional centers collect from each investor (travel, marketing, legal fees, sales commissions), repeated from the OIG's December 2013 audit (OIG-14-19). Not set by government.

observations.location: p. 5, Background (A. The EB-5 Program), lines 2-3
observations.quote: The Act allocates 9,940 immigrant visas each fiscal year to foreign nationals participating in the EB-5 program
observations.notes: Annual EB-5 visa allocation as described by the court (citing 8 U.S.C. 1151(d), 1153(b)(5)); a statutory ceiling, not an outturn. Dated to the order (22 June 2021) because the court gives no fiscal year; the statute sets the EB-5 share as a percentage of the employment-based limit, so the number varies by year.

observations.location: p. 5, Background (A. The EB-5 Program), lines 3-4
observations.quote: and at least 3,000 of the visas must be reserved for persons investing in TEAs
observations.notes: Minimum annual reservation for investors in targeted employment areas ('at least 3,000'), as described by the court (pre-2022 law).

observations.location: p. 3, Background
observations.quote: more than 600 regional centers operated throughout the country as of 2021.
observations.notes: 'More than 600', a lower bound, stated by the court (no source given). The order also calls them '600-plus previously authorized regional centers' (p. 1) when the 2022 Act took effect.

observations.location: p. 5, Background
observations.quote: USCIS interprets the Integrity Act as setting a nonbinding target date of six months by which the agency should process any new I‑956
observations.notes: A target, not an outturn: USCIS's reading of the 2022 Act (sec. 106(b)) as a non-binding six-month target for deciding new Form I-956 regional center applications, as described by the court.

observations.location: paragraph 1
observations.notes: AnC Vermont (Jay Peak) EB-5 project: restitution the court ordered Ariel Quiros to pay at sentencing on 29 April 2022 (adjudicated). Not a programme-wide total; the scheme raised about $85 million from about 169 investors in 2012-2016. '$' in a US Department of Justice release.

observations.location: paragraph 4
observations.quote: Quiros admitted using AnC investor funds for personal expenses, specifically a $6 million payment to the IRS in early 2015 funded by a loan collateralized by investor funds
observations.notes: AnC Vermont (Jay Peak) EB-5 project: misuse admitted by Quiros in his guilty plea (August 2020) - a personal tax payment in early 2015 funded by a loan secured on investor funds. Case-level, not a programme total.

program_terms.applies_to: corporate sponsor, per employee (Trump Corporate Gold Card; transferable to a new employee)
program_terms.location: FAQ 'What is the Trump Corporate Gold Card?'
program_terms.quote: A $2 million per employee gift upon completion of the employee’s vetting is evidence that the employee will substantially benefit the United States.
program_terms.notes: The gift tied to one employee can be reused to sponsor a new employee without a new $2 million gift. As stated on trumpcard.gov (undated government page, saved 2 Oct 2026); valid_from left empty because the page gives no date.

program_terms.applies_to: per person: individual applicant, each family member, each sponsored employee (non-refundable DHS processing fee)
program_terms.location: Home page and FAQ 'What is the Trump Gold Card?'
program_terms.quote: To apply, an applicant must pay a nonrefundable, $15,000 DHS processing fee.
program_terms.notes: Corporate: '$15,000 DHS processing fee per employee'. Small additional State Department visa fees may apply. As stated on trumpcard.gov (undated government page, saved 2 Oct 2026); valid_from left empty because the page gives no date.

program_terms.applies_to: Trump Corporate Gold Card, per year
program_terms.location: FAQ 'What is the Trump Corporate Gold Card?'
program_terms.quote: The Trump Corporate Gold Card is subject to a small, 1% annual maintenance fee and a 5% transfer fee
program_terms.notes: The page does not say what the 1% is charged on (presumably the gift). Not in Executive Order 14351. As stated on trumpcard.gov (undated government page, saved 2 Oct 2026); valid_from left empty because the page gives no date.

program_terms.applies_to: Trump Corporate Gold Card, per transfer to a new employee (includes a new DHS background check)
program_terms.location: FAQ 'What is the Trump Corporate Gold Card?'
program_terms.quote: The Trump Corporate Gold Card is subject to a small, 1% annual maintenance fee and a 5% transfer fee, which includes the cost of a new DHS background check.
program_terms.notes: The page does not say what the 5% is charged on. Not in Executive Order 14351. As stated on trumpcard.gov (undated government page, saved 2 Oct 2026); valid_from left empty because the page gives no date.

events.description: The regional center programme stops being called a pilot; its authorisation was then due to expire on 30 September 2015.

events.title: USCIS opens the Immigrant Investor Program Office in Washington
events.description: Announced on 3 December 2012, the new headquarters office devoted to EB-5 adjudications opened on 6 May 2013, staffed with economists and officers with business and legal expertise plus fraud and national-security staff; EB-5 work moved there from the California Service Center.

new_indicators.name: Applications to designate an investment-pooling entity approved
new_indicators.definition: Applications for designation (or amendment) of an intermediary entity that pools investor money (e.g. US EB-5 regional center, Forms I-924 / I-956) approved by the programme authority in a period.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-cbi-usa1 (DHS OIG-14-19, FY2012). Not investor petitions: those are applications_approved.

new_indicators.name: Applications to designate an investment-pooling entity denied
new_indicators.definition: Applications for designation (or amendment) of an intermediary entity that pools investor money (e.g. US EB-5 regional center) denied by the programme authority in a period.

new_indicators.name: Applications to designate an investment-pooling entity filed
new_indicators.definition: Applications for designation or amendment of an intermediary entity that pools investor money (e.g. US EB-5 regional center, Forms I-924 / I-956) filed in a period; unit regional_centers when the source counts entities that filed rather than filings.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-cbi-usa1 (DHS OIG-14-19: 336 regional centers with I-924 filings FY2010-FY2012).

new_indicators.name: Intermediary fees charged per investor
new_indicators.definition: Fees that private intermediaries (e.g. US EB-5 regional centers, agents) charge each investor on top of the qualifying investment, as reported by an authority; often a range.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-cbi-usa1 (DHS OIG-14-19: regional center fees of $25,000-$50,000 per investor). Not set by government, so not a programme term.

new_indicators.name: Processing time for a decision
new_indicators.definition: Time the programme authority publishes (or an official body reports) for deciding a type of application, in months, at a date; say in notes whether it is a median, an average or the time within which most cases are decided.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-cbi-usa1 (USCIS EB-5 wait times for Forms I-526, I-829 and I-924, January 2015, in DHS OIG 2015). Use breakdown form=.

ledger.contains: Report of the Visa Office 2005, Table V: immigrant visas issued abroad plus adjustments of status subject to numerical limits, FY2005, by foreign state of chargeability (every country and dependent area, with dependent-area TOTAL rows where printed, region totals and grand totals). The table is marked "Preliminary data - subject to change". EB-5 columns: 5th Employment Creation, 5th Target Employment Areas, 5th Regional Pilot Program, 5th Regional Target Areas, 5th Total. Extracted: the 5th Total for every row (including zeros), and the four class columns for every row whose 5th Total is not zero and for every TOTAL, region and grand-total row; rows with 5th Total 0 print 0 in all four class columns, so those zero class cells are not recorded separately. DHS Office of Homeland Security Statistics, Yearbook of Immigration Statistics 2023, Lawful Permanent Residents workbook (TOC plus Tables 1-12 and Supplemental Tables 1-4). In scope: Table 6 row 'Fifth: Employment creation (investors)' FY2014-FY2023 in the TOTAL, ADJUSTMENTS OF STATUS and NEW ARRIVALS blocks (30 values, already in the data), and Table 7 (FY2023) 'Fifth: Employment creation (investors)' total (11930 / 1480 / 10440, same as Table 6, already in the data) and its 24 detailed class rows (C51-C58, E56/E57/E53, I51-I58, T51-T58, R51/R52/R53: principal, spouse and child, new arrival or adjustment), now extracted. Table 7 cells are rounded to tens: the 24 detailed rows add to 11900 against the printed total 11930 (adjustments 1480 and new arrivals 10440 add up within rounding too), a rounding difference the table's own note warns about. Out of scope: all other classes of admission, and Tables 1-5 and 8-12 and the supplemental tables, which give country of birth/last residence, state, CBSA, age, sex and occupation only for all LPRs or for broad classes ('Employment-based preferences'), with no EB-5 split.

DHS Office of Immigration Statistics, 2013 Yearbook of Immigration Statistics (122 pages): LPR Tables 1-12, refugees and asylees Tables 13-19, naturalizations Tables 20-24, nonimmigrant admissions Tables 25-32, enforcement Tables 33-41. In scope: Table 6 (PDF pp. 23-24) row 'Fifth: Employment creation (investors)' FY2004-FY2013 in the TOTAL block (10 values, already in the data), the ADJUSTMENTS OF STATUS and NEW ARRIVALS blocks (20 values, now extracted; adjustments plus new arrivals equal the total in every year), and Table 7 (FY2013, PDF pp. 27-28) EB-5 total (8,543 / 1,231 / 7,312, same as Table 6) and its detailed class rows (C51-C58, I51-I58, T51-T58, R51-R57): 17 printed values extracted (of 22 class rows); 5 rows (R51, R56, C57, R57, R53) are 'D', withheld by DHS and have no value. The printed class rows add to 8,508; the 35 difference from 8,543 is in the withheld D cells. Out of scope: other classes of admission; LPR tables by country, state, CBSA and demographics give only all-class or broad-class ('Employment-based preferences') figures; nonimmigrant tables count treaty investors (E-2), a different, non-immigrant category; refugees, naturalization and enforcement tables.

DHS OIG audit report OIG-14-19 (12 Dec 2013, 40 pages) on the EB-5 Regional Center Program: findings, four recommendations, Appendix A (scope), Appendix B (USCIS management comments of 4 Nov 2013, a scan with an imperfect text layer), contributors, distribution. Programme numbers: 325 approved regional centers at 1 Oct 2013 (already in the data); USCIS's unsupported cumulative figures since 1990 (more than $6.8 billion invested, at least 49,000 jobs); FY2012 regional center applications approved (35) and denied (63); 336 regional centers with I-924 filings in FY2010-FY2012; regional-center fees of $25,000-$50,000 per investor - all now extracted. Rule and timeline items added as events: 'pilot' dropped 3 Aug 2012, Form I-924 required from 2010, annual I-924A from 2011, policy memorandum 30 May 2013 (the report's own release is already an event). The opening of the Immigrant Investor Program Office (May 2013, Appendix B) is recorded as an event from usa-dhsoig-eb5-mayorkas-2015, which gives the exact day. The $500,000 / $1 million minimum investment is restated as background and is already in program_terms from the statute and regulations. Out of scope: single-case audit findings (12 of 15 files reviewed, a project 82% funded by US investors, a hotel costing about $28 million with $4.5 million of foreign money), audit sample sizes (15 regional center files, 6 investor files, 22 cases), and USCIS staffing (9 EB-5 staff in 2009, more than 80 in 2013, 7 then 9 economists, 22 economists).

DHS OIG investigation report (24 Mar 2015, 99 pages) into employee complaints about Director Mayorkas's handling of EB-5 matters: summary, background on the programme and petition process, three case narratives (LA Films, Las Vegas/SLS, Gulf Coast), timelines (Appendices A-B) and Mr. Mayorkas's 32-page statement (Appendix C, a scan). Programme numbers, all now extracted: about 641 regional centers approved at 2 Mar 2015; FY2012 I-526 petitions filed (6,041) and approved (3,677) and I-829 approvals (736) - all three match the USCIS data already in the dataset; USCIS wait times at January 2015 (I-526 14.2, I-829 12.3, I-924 11.7 months); more than 700 regional center applications 'in the three years in question' (years not stated); regional-center fees of $25,000-$50,000 per investor; and, as a rule, the $6,230 regional center application fee charged from the 2010 fee rule (Appendix C). Event added: Immigrant Investor Program Office opened 6 May 2013 (the report itself is already an event). The $500,000 / $1 million minimum and the 10-job requirement are restated background, already in program_terms from primary sources. Out of scope: case-level figures (more than 200 LA Films III petitions, 240/249 LA Films IV petitions, about 230 SLS investors of whom 47 had filed by 23 Jan 2013, Gulf Coast $555,000 units), investigation statistics (about 50 interviews, more than 40,000 call records, more than 15 witnesses), and USCIS-wide figures (about 19,000 staff, 223 offices, 6,100 green cards and 3,200 naturalisations a day, 2007 fee rise of about 86%).

Order of the US District Court, N.D. Cal. (22 June 2021, 17 pages) in Behring Regional Center LLC v. Wolf granting summary judgment: background on the EB-5 programme and the 2019 Modernization Rule, analysis under the Federal Vacancies Reform Act, and vacatur of the rule (already an event). Programme numbers: the annual allocation of 9,940 EB-5 visas with at least 3,000 reserved for targeted employment areas (now extracted as planned places, status budget). Rules restated from statute and the 2019 rule ($1,000,000 standard / $500,000 TEA minimum; $1.8 million / $900,000 under the 2019 rule; TEA = rural area or unemployment of at least 150% of the national average; rural = outside a metropolitan area or town of 20,000 or more) are already in program_terms from the statute and Federal Register. Other numbers are dates and legal citations.

Order of the US District Court, N.D. Cal. (24 June 2022, 14 pages) in Behring Regional Center LLC v. Mayorkas granting a preliminary injunction: USCIS may not treat regional centers designated before the EB-5 Reform and Integrity Act of 2022 as deauthorized (already an event). Programme numbers: more than 600 regional centers operating as of 2021 / '600-plus' when the Act took effect (now extracted once, as of 2021). The six-month non-binding target for deciding new I-956 applications is extracted as a processing-time target (status budget). Rules and dates restated (pilot programme of 1992 with a 1997 sunset, lapse June 2021, Act effective 15 March 2022, authorisation to September 2027) are already in the programme notes and events. Out of scope: 'over 100 regional centers' represented by an amicus seeking to intervene (case-level), case-management dates.

trumpcard.gov home page and FAQ (Department of Commerce), saved 2 Oct 2026. Not about EB-5: describes the Gold Card (usa-gold-card). Rules now extracted as program_terms from this page: $1 million gift (individual and each family member), $2 million per employee (corporate), $15,000 non-refundable DHS processing fee per person, 1% annual maintenance fee and 5% transfer fee for corporate cards. The 'Trump Platinum Card' ($5 million contribution plus $15,000 fee, up to 270 days a year without US tax on non-US income) is only announced ('Coming Soon', waitlist) and has no programme row; it is already recorded as an event. No counts of applications, approvals or money received are given ('wait times of up to a year or more' for some countries is not a figure).

DOJ (US Attorney, District of Vermont) press release of 29 April 2022 on the sentencing of Ariel Quiros in the AnC Vermont / Jay Peak EB-5 fraud (already an event). Case-level money figures extracted as investor funds misused: restitution of $8,338,600.77 ordered and the admitted $6 million personal tax payment funded with a loan secured on investor funds. Other case figures (planned $110 million from 220 investors; about 169 investors, about $85 million invested and about $8 million in administrative fees in 2012-2016; 60-month, 18-month and 97-month-cap sentences) describe the case and are in the event description where relevant; they are not programme statistics and have no matching indicator. Related-content links at the foot of the page are unrelated.

DOJ (US Attorney, C.D. Cal.) press release of 27 Nov 2017: attorney Victoria Chan pleads guilty in the California Investment Immigration Fund EB-5 scheme (already an event). Figures: more than $50 million collected from more than 100 mainly Chinese investors, about 130 fraudulent EB-5 applications, eight properties worth nearly $25 million to be forfeited, homes worth nearly $1 million each bought with 'hundreds of thousands of dollars' of investor funds, 45-year statutory maximum. Case-level figures describe the case and are in the existing event's description where relevant; they are not programme statistics and match no indicator (no amount of investor money misused is stated). Programme rules restated in the release (minimum investment of $500,000, 10 new jobs) are already in program_terms from primary sources. Related-content links at the foot of the page are unrelated.

DOJ (US Attorney, C.D. Cal.) press release of 10 Jan 2017: Shilan Zhao pleads guilty to conspiring to commit immigration fraud in her EB-5 application (false marriage certificate and source-of-funds documents) (already an event). Figures: $25,000 bond to be applied to restitution, forfeiture of several properties (no values), five-year statutory maximum. Case-level figures describe the case and are in the existing event's description where relevant; they are not programme statistics and match no indicator (no amount of investor money misused is stated). Related-content links at the foot of the page are unrelated.

DOJ (US Attorney, E.D. La.) press release of 22 June 2021: operators of the New Orleans EB-5 Regional Center sentenced to 102 months each (already an event). Figures: 31 immigrants invested $15.5 million ($500,000 each in a targeted employment area) plus service fees; $18,070,000 obtained from all investors including one non-immigrant; funds 'fraudulently misappropriated' but no amount stated; restitution left for later. Case-level figures describe the case and are in the existing event's description where relevant; they are not programme statistics and match no indicator (no amount of investor money misused is stated). Programme rules restated in the release (minimum investment $1,000,000 / $500,000 in targeted employment areas, 10 jobs, two-year conditional residence) are already in program_terms from primary sources. Related-content links at the foot of the page are unrelated.

DOJ (US Attorney, N.D. Cal.) press release of 22 July 2021: Thomas Henderson (San Francisco Regional Center) and Cooper Lee plead guilty (already an event). Figures: SFRC raised more than $100 million from foreign investors for seven EB-5 enterprises in 2011-2017; funds from 42 investors in North America 3PL LP used for other projects (amount not stated); statutory maximum penalties. Case-level figures describe the case and are in the existing event's description where relevant; they are not programme statistics and match no indicator (no amount of investor money misused is stated). Programme rules restated in the release (minimum investment $1,000,000 / $500,000 in targeted employment areas, 10 jobs, two-year conditional residence) are already in program_terms from primary sources. Related-content links at the foot of the page are unrelated.
